source_identity.title: The steady states of strong-KPP reactions in general domains

problems.title: The basepoint-component spectral label need not define an open set

location.locator: Theorem 4.3; Lemma 4.4; (4.7); definition of Omega_+^0 and continuity assertion; (4.14); dependence of Theorem 1.1

problems.decisive_evidence: For R=10 and g(x)=sqrt(400-x^2), choose compactly supported smooth h with h(0)=-1,h(-1)>g(-1), h<g on [0,7] except h=g-(x-1)^2 near 1, and h=-3 on [3,7]. The uniformly smooth epigraph Omega={y>h(x)} has limit spectrum {0}. The component C_0 of Omega intersect B20(0) containing 0 lies in the strip -1<x<1 and has lambda>=pi^2/4. For centers z_epsilon=(0,epsilon), epsilon>0, the upper arc g+epsilon opens the contact at x=1; C_epsilon contains the square (3,7)x(-2,2), so lambda<=pi^2/8. Set mu=3pi^2/16 and delta=pi^2/64; the spectral gap holds, lambda(B1)/100<=pi^2/100<delta, while mu+delta=13pi^2/64 lies strictly between the two bounds. Thus 0 belongs to Omega_+^0 but arbitrarily close z_epsilon do not.
problems.impact: The required openness is false under the actual gap and regularity hypotheses. Lemma 4.4 cannot be applied as written, and smooth convergence of original domains does not justify convergence of selected ball components before (4.14). This is a central gap in the decomposition proof used by general uniqueness.
problems.repair_boundary: A stable localization/open-label construction and new proofs of coverage, narrow spectral control and ample limit inequalities are needed. A continuity citation or changing one fixed radius is insufficient.
problems.counterevidence_and_scope: Not a counterexample to Theorems 4.3 or 1.1: this particular epigraph has a trivial ample decomposition. The demonstration is analytic and requires no thin-neck spectral limit or numerical eigenvalue computation.
problems.attribution: Principal proposed and evaluated construction; native proof auxiliary independently checked geometry, spectrum and constants. The theorem auxiliary checked constants and scope.

problems.title: Positive eigenfunctions cannot be selected on all components at the smallest component eigenvalue

location.locator: Disconnected-domain convention; Proposition 2.1(iii)-(iv); normalized phi_R; related hair-trigger selection

problems.decisive_evidence: Two bounded Dirichlet components with lambda1>lambda2 cannot carry a strictly positive eigenfunction at lambda2 on both: testing the first component against its positive ground state gives (lambda1-lambda2) integral(phi psi1)=0. The Problem 1 smooth connected epigraph produces such unequal components after the ball cut.
problems.impact: The printed globally positive normalized phi_R selection is not valid for an arbitrary ball truncation.
problems.repair_boundary: Use the increasing basepoint component D_R, which exhausts the connected original domain, prove its eigenvalue limit through normalized Harnack compactness and generalized-eigenvalue comparison, then squeeze the whole-truncation eigenvalue between lambda(Omega) and lambda(D_R). For nonlinear subsolutions select a low-eigenvalue component and extend by zero.
problems.counterevidence_and_scope: The intended exhaustion conclusion is not refuted; p.18 already uses a component selection compatible with the local repair.

problems.title: The initial constant upper envelope must be at least one

location.locator: Proposition 1.8 proof and (4.24); M=sup v(0); multiplicity construction under (P)

problems.decisive_evidence: In a bounded Robin weak-KPP multiplicity example, let u_L have sup<1/2 and u_H sup>1/2. Hopf gives m=min_closure u_L>0. For v0=epsilon u_L with epsilon<m/||u_L||infty, M=epsilon||u_L||infty<m, hence P_t M<=u_L for all t. But P_infty 1=u_+>=u_H exceeds u_L somewhere, contradicting the asserted equality P_infty M=P_infty 1.
problems.impact: The identification of the upper envelope is false at the proof stage assuming only positive reaction.
problems.repair_boundary: Set M=max(1,sup v0); this is a supersolution, its decreasing limit is at most one and comparison with P_t1 identifies it with u_+.
problems.counterevidence_and_scope: Uses the multiplicity construction with the corrected Robin energy; does not presume convergence from an arbitrary small constant. The intended hair-trigger upper bound survives the repair.

independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: A positive low Robin equilibrium has positive closure minimum m. Choosing v0=epsilon uL with sup v0<m traps P_t M below uL, whereas P_infty1>=uH exceeds it. Thus the printed equality fails under only positivity.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: When M<=1 comparison with P_t1 proves the required upper bound without equality; when M>1 the supersolution limit identification applies.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_scope: M=max(1,sup v0) or the direct comparison case split restores the intended bound, not a new global convergence theorem.

independent_acceptance_scope.result: All four reported defects are supported in the exact author version. P1 is a demonstrated failure of the open spectral label on the decomposition proof chain; P2?P4 remain local auxiliary errors with the limitations below. No counterexample to the uniqueness or decomposition theorem itself is established.
counterevidence_and_severity_basis: P1 is Major because Lemma4.4 requires the open set whose asserted openness fails, and the uniqueness proof invokes Theorem4.3.

P2 concerns positive eigenfunction selection on a disconnected truncation, while the increasing basepoint component restores the same exhaustion argument. No final connected-domain eigenfunction/exhaustion conclusion is refuted.
For P3 the printed minimizer still obeys partial_nu u+a u=-a u<=0 and therefore supplies the subsolution actually needed downstream; the exact solution identification is wrong.
For P4, when M<=1 the needed upper inequality follows directly from P_t M<=P_t 1; the stronger equality is unnecessary. This actual dependency, not repair length, limits impact.
